title: GPU rack density scenario planning Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This planning sheet evaluates three rack-density deployment scenarios for on-prem and colocation GPU pools. Focus: per-rack power and cooling, usable GPU slot counts, floor-tile load, corridor clearance constraints, and phased delivery windows for Q4 2026 – Q2 2027.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SRE/Platform, Data Center ops, Solutions engineering, Facilities leads
- Sites: primary focus on two target colo rooms (us-west-2a primary, eu-west-1 secondary) plus a small on-prem EU pilot (customer POC room C).
- Hardware targets: 4U node with 4x H100 SXM5 equivalent, alternate 2U with 2x GPU for higher-density corridors.

Key assumptions (inputs):
- Tile rating: 150 lb/ft^2 (structural ok up to 250 lb/ft^2 with reinforcement)
- Rack footprint: 24in x 48in per standard cabinet (0.78 m^2)
- Typical full-load power per high-density rack (8 x 4U nodes): 24 kW nominal, 30 kW peak contingency
- Alternate mid-density rack (12 x 2U nodes): 12 kW nominal, 15 kW peak
- CRAC capacity per unit: 60 kW sensible cooling each (N+1 plan: 3 units per room for 120 kW usable continuous)
- PUE target: 1.25 for new colos, 1.4 for on-prem pilot
- Average utilization target for capacity planning: 65% (headroom for burst -> plan for 85% saturation capability without thermal violation)

Scenario summaries (high-level):
1) Conservative (spaced racks, low density)
   - Rack type: mid-density 12kW nominal
   - Racks per 1000 ft^2 usable: 28
   - Usable GPUs per 1000 ft^2: ~336 (12U-equivalent GPU slots)
   - Room power draw per 1000 ft^2: ~336 kW peak (includes PDUs, practice: treat as 1.1x for overhead)
   - Cooling margin: ~20% under CRAC N+1
   - Notes: easier airflow management, lower single-rack failure blast radius, higher floor usage (less GPUs per sqft)

2) Baseline (balanced density) – recommended default for rollout
   - Rack type: mixed (50% high-density, 50% mid-density)
   - Effective nominal rack power: 18 kW avg
   - Racks per 1000 ft^2: 36
   - Usable GPUs per 1000 ft^2: ~864 (based on node counts, not raw card counts; includes accessory/networking)
   - Room power draw per 1000 ft^2: ~650 kW peak (includes 10% overhead for PDUs & switch gear)
   - Cooling margin: ~10% under planned CRAC capacity – requires monitoring and dynamic load shaping
   - Notes: best trade-off of density vs ops risk; requires strict PDU balancing and thermal mapping pre-staging

3) Aggressive (maximum density)
   - Rack type: high-density 24–30 kW racks (30 kW peak planned)
   - Racks per 1000 ft^2: 44 (tight hot/cold aisle, in-row cooling recommended)
   - Usable GPUs per 1000 ft^2: ~2048 (maximum consolidation)
   - Room power draw per 1000 ft^2: ~1.3 MW peak (likely exceeds standard CRAC capacity; needs in-row or direct liquid cooling and floor reinforcement)
   - Cooling margin: negative without additional infrastructure (requires water-loop heat exchangers or immersion)
   - Notes: only for sites with robust power and chilled water; increases ops complexity and failure blast radius

Tile-level load & structural check quick calc (example):
- Single high-density rack footprint occupies ~4 floor tiles (2x2). 30 kW rack -> distributed load ~7.5 kW per tile -> convert to lb/ft^2 = ~185 lb/ft^2 (requires reinforced tile or contained plinth)
- Action: tag racks >20 kW for structural sign-off and raised-floor reinforcement request (ticket INFRA-1399).

Corridor & aisle planning notes:
- Maintain minimum 42in cold aisle clearance for hardware mobility and fire code; 48in preferred for 30 kW racks with hand trucks.
- Staging zones: 1 10ft x 14ft unpack and pre-config station per 20 racks (powered temp PDUs, floor absorbent mats).
- Cable routing: overhead tray required for power > 20 kW per rack to avoid underfloor cable congestion.

Power distribution & PDU strategy:
- Use dual-feed A/B PDUs with staggered phase assignments per rack to smooth facility demand spikes.
- For racks >20 kW, split critical circuits across separate UPS strings; do not co-locate elastically-scheduled maintenance windows on racks sharing same bus.
- Recommend inline branch monitoring (per-outlet) on every high-density rack.

Thermal mapping guidance (pre-deploy checklist):
- Step 1: baseline IR scan with empty racks and with representative load (50% nodes powered)
- Step 2: install per-rack inlet temp sensors and telemetry ingestion to Console (route: "telemetry/thermal/<room>")
- Step 3: run 72-hour soak test at 85% utilization with staggered stress to observe temperature swing and PDU currents

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Hotspot runaway: implement automatic workload shedding and immediate fallbacks to another region if inlet temp > 38C for 10 minutes.
- PDU trip: deploy rapid-redeploy playbook with spare network switch, spare PSU sets, and imaging container; mark racks for reduced load until repair.

Region-specific notes (us-west-2 vs eu-west-1):
- us-west-2: colo rooms have 480V buss available; simpler to provision step-down transformers and larger PDUs; recommended baseline density here.
- eu-west-1: several facilities are older raised-floor designs with limited CRAC redundancy; prefer conservative or hybrid deployments and plan for in-row cooling addition.

Phasing and timeline (proposal):
- Phase 0 (Aug–Sep 2026): Detailed thermal simulation and structural sign-offs for both target colos (deliver infra spec package)
- Phase 1 (Oct–Dec 2026): Pilot 20 racks (mixed density) in us-west-2; run soak tests & production-like workloads; validate autoscaling/batching impact on thermal patterns
- Phase 2 (Jan–Mar 2027): Expand to 100 racks baseline mix; enable PDU per-outlet monitoring and telemetry dashboards
- Phase 3 (Apr–Jun 2027): Evaluate aggressive density for limited corridor (choose 10 racks for in-row cooling); decision gate based on 60-day steady-state temp and power headroom

Cost & procurement quick notes:
- Anticipated CAPEX uplift for reinforced floor + in-row cooling modules for aggressive sites: $450–700k per room (site dependent)
- Incremental OPEX: cooling + power at 1.25 PUE adds 25% overhead to compute power draw; budget projection included in linked sheet (Confluence link above).

Immediate next actions (owners & tickets):
- INFRA-1399 (Priya) -> structural floor reinforcement scoping and vendor quote (due 2026-07-26)
- INFRA-1402 (Liam) -> order per-rack power monitoring PDUs for pilot (20 units) (due 2026-08-05)
- SRE-2121 (Evan) -> thermal telemetry ingestion pipeline + dashboard (due 2026-08-15)
- Solutions-0037 (Sofia) -> customer pilot coordination and on-prem room prep checklist (due 2026-08-01)

Decisions required by 2026-08-01:
- Accept baseline mixed-density as default for new colos? (Y/N)
- Commit to overhead budget for floor reinforcement at eu-west-1? (attach CFO sign-off if yes)

Appendices (short):
- Quick heat conversion: 1 kW ~ 3412 BTU/hr. A 30 kW rack -> ~102k BTU/hr.
- Emergency coolant options: in-row glycol chiller, warm-water loop, direct-to-chip plates (immersion is out-of-scope for baseline).
- Sample telemetry fields to collect: inlet_temp_C, outlet_temp_C, PDU_total_kW, per_outlet_amp, fan_rpm, cabinet_vibration_g, job_id, model_variant

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is intentionally light on exact GPU counts; we want to iterate against actual purchase SKUs (H100 vs H200 vs 4x A100) and partner site constraints.
- Please annotate Confluence page with any local colo limitations (CRAC age, water loop availability).

Checklist before next review meeting (2026-07-22):
- [ ] Structural vendor shortlist (3) attached to INFRA-1399
- [ ] PDU vendor quotes in PRD (Liam)
- [ ] Pilot rack inventory and serial mapping ready (SRE team)
- [ ] Room-level CRAC & electrical schematics uploaded to Confluence

End of sheet.
